data.name: Saraswatha
data.gender_notes: Saraswatha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Saraswatha is the Hindu goddess of knowledge, music, art, wisdom, and learning. She is depicted as a beautiful woman with four arms. The name Saraswatha carries the meaning “Goddess of knowledge and wisdom” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Saraswatha usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of knowledge and wisdom and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name symbolizes the power of knowledge and wisdom to transform one's life.
data.etymology: Saraswatha belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of knowledge and wisdom.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Saraswatha total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Saraswathi is revered as the Goddess of Knowledge, Arts, learning, Music, and Wisdom in Hindu tradition. In the wider Indian society, the worship of Saraswati is believed to bring prosperity, enlightenment, and good fortune. In many Indian households, particularly among scholars and artists, the goddess Saraswati is invoked before starting any new work.
data.spiritual_significance: Saraswati represents the purity of the mind and the power to impart knowledge to all those who seek it. She is believed to bestow upon her devotees the ability to learn and understand new concepts, to communicate effectively, and to create beautiful, meaningful works of art. In meditation and practice, she embodies the qualities of purity, dignity, and selfless dedication to knowledge and the arts.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Saraswathi symbolizes knowledge, learning, and wisdom. She is the embodiment of the sacred Veda and the goddess of music and arts. Her name, derived from the Saras or 'river', signifies the flow of knowledge and enlightenment.

vedic_reference.note: From the Rigveda, Saraswatha is the goddess of knowledge, music, art, wisdom, and learning.

historical_references.reference: Goddess Saraswati is associated with music, knowledge, wisdom, and arts. She is depicted as seated on a lotus with a veena in her hands, signifying music and knowledge.
historical_references.context: Saraswati is a major deity in Hinduism and is considered the goddess of knowledge, learning, wisdom, and the arts. She is often invoked before starting any learning process.

historical_references.reference: Saraswati is also identified with the Vedic river of the same name, considered to be the personification of the sacred waters of learning and wisdom.
historical_references.context: In the ancient Indian texts, the river Saraswati is described as the goddess Saraswati herself, whose waters represent knowledge and wisdom.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Hindu goddess Saraswathi is revered for her knowledge, wisdom, and creativity. In modern times, her name is seen on various digital platforms. Google Doodle often features Saraswathi on her Vasant Panchami day, celebrating her as the goddess of knowledge. Instagram users often post pictures of Saraswathi idols, flowers, and books during the festival of Saraswathi Puja. Pinterest sees a surge in pins related to Saraswathi, her symbols, and her festivals.

name_in_real_life.story: Lakshmi Saraswatha from Kolkata, India embodies the meaning of Saraswatha - "Goddess of knowledge and wisdom". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.
